Strike · Bulgaria

Bulgaria reports drone strike on ship CHELSEA 3 off Byala; crew rescued

13 October 2026 · Off Byala · CHELSEA 3 drone strike

Officially reported aerial-drone strike and rescue; operator unresolved

Overnight on 13 October 2026 the Maltese-flagged merchant ship CHELSEA 3 was struck by drones in the Black Sea, reportedly 18 nautical miles east of Byala in Varna Province, within Bulgaria’s exclusive economic zone and outside its territorial waters. According to the crew’s account, relayed by Bulgaria’s prime minister, three aerial drones hit the deck and hull. A distress notification reached Varna’s maritime rescue centre at 01:30 local time.

The operator and nationality are unresolved. Radev said the evidence was insufficient to accuse either belligerent; he argued that the attacks benefit Russia, but that argument and planned diplomatic consultations do not establish Russian responsibility. The ship is reportedly Ukrainian-owned and registered in Odessa, which is separate from the question of who attacked it.

Border Police evacuated all 15 crew, seven Ukrainians and eight Azerbaijanis, who were brought to Varna; five were treated for initially reported minor injuries, and no deaths were reported. The ship was damaged and its final condition is unconfirmed. On the same day, another vessel was reported struck and sunk east of Krapets.

Attribution and uncertainty

Origin / operator / attribution
Operator and nationality unresolved. Radev said evidence was insufficient to accuse either belligerent. His argument that the attacks benefit Russia and planned diplomatic consultations do not establish Russian responsibility.
Investigation / uncertainty
High confidence in the published official strike/rescue account; no independently examined drone remains or flight tracks. Weapon identity and ship outcome remain pending. Nationality of crew, ship flag, ownership and attacker are separate facts.
